requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. This citation is optional;
helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.util` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. I checked each clause for a behavior-preserving alternative that would violate it:

- "Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text". This requires that the name resolves and has the quoted fixed text. The built-in could be stored in a Rust constant, a bundled markdown file or a generated table. Each gives the same resolution result and text, so where the definition lives is discretionary. The general mechanism for resolving `habeas:<name>` belongs to `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which is cited here for context and is not the subject.
- "Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary." This is a rule about which reference roles validation accepts. It is observable: `{impl}`, `{test}` or `{fixme}` references to it are rejected, and `{cite}` references are accepted. It prescribes no particular check structure.
- "An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review under `requirements.references.citation_review`." This is the exemption from review requirements. It is observable in validation output: no missing-review report appears for such items. It prescribes no structure.
- "This citation is optional; helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code." This is permissive and imposes nothing structural.

The review roots are empty and no acknowledgments were supplied. Every clause specifies observable behavior, so there are no implementation roots to find or assess.

behavioral: The subject has four behavioral obligations. The reviewed tests cover each one.

1. **Built-in `habeas:util` exists with the stated text.**
   - `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` resolves `builtin("habeas:util")`.
   - It asserts the text's start and end.
   - It asserts the text equals the block quote in `md/reference.md`, which covers the requirement that the reference documentation includes the text.
   - `Builtin::text` builds the text from the requirement's own quote in `md/requirements/references.md`, using `quoted_text(chapter, ":::{req} util")`. The text therefore cannot drift from the requirement without the quote changing.
   - The same test shows `habeas:none` and `habeas:other` are not resolved as built-ins.

2. **Only `{cite}` may reference it.**
   - The builtins test asserts `check(Cite)` succeeds. It asserts `check(Impl)` and `check(Test)` return the error that the built-in may only be referenced with `{cite}`.
   - `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` writes `{impl}` and `{test}` references to `habeas:util` and asserts the validation error for each.
   - `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` asserts the same error for a fenced `{impl}` reference.

3. **Inline or fenced citations, with or without commentary, are permitted.**
   - The `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item...` test uses an inline citation (`inline`), a fenced citation with commentary (`fenced`) and a fenced citation without commentary (`bare`). It asserts none of them produces an error.
   - The `fenced_references_in_comments...` test covers fenced citations with commentary (`glue`).
   - `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_groups_nested_citations_but_excludes_declarations_and_literals]` shows that fenced `habeas:util` citations in book commentary are accepted as citations.

4. **An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` needs no citation review.**
   - The `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item...` test asserts there is no "missing citation review" for `inline`, `fenced` and `bare`.
   - The same test covers the converse case. The `mixed` item also cites `rules.ready`, and the test asserts it still needs a review.
   - The `fenced_references_in_comments...` test asserts `glue` needs no review while `empty` (which also cites `rules.ready`) does.
   - The `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item...` test also asserts that no `evidence/habeas:util` record is required.

The last sentence of the requirement says the citation is optional. That imposes no testable obligation.

text: :::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. This citation is optional;
helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST resolve built-in names of the form `habeas:<name>` alongside project
definitions in every project without a project declaration. Each built-in MUST
specify its permitted reference roles and have fixed text stating its obligations.
Habeas's reference documentation MUST include that text.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
